messages:
morgan: Quick onboarding check for flan-2x into Dedicated pool — want to validate weights location, tokenizer gotcha, and final serving knobs before canary. Posting all notes here so we have an async trail.

kai: Weights uploaded to s3://redwood-models/flan-2x/v1/weights.tar.gz — SHA256: 9f3a...d2c. I ran `aws s3 ls` and checksum locally matches.

sara: tokenizer note: the HF tokenizer for flan-2x uses a legacy EOS id (2) but our eval prompts assume </s>=50256. You can either remap `eos_token_id` or set `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token':'</s>'})` when loading. TL;DR: mismatch causes off-by-one truncation at max_tokens.

ryan: thanks — important. For serving config I'm thinking conservative defaults for canary:
```
continuous_batching: true
max_batch_tokens: 16384   # global token cap per batch
max_batch_size: 24
kv_cache_enabled: true
cache_policy:
  prefix_cache: true
  ttl_seconds: 120
scheduler:
  preemptive_eviction: false
  slot_timeout_ms: 150
```
This keeps latency predictable while still batching. Thoughts?

anika: Suggest `max_generated_tokens` override to protect long requests — set `max_total_tokens: 4096` at first. Also add `reject_on_overflow: true` so we don't spill to slow tier.

morgan: +1 on conservative token caps. Will add a rollout policy: 5% traffic canary on dedicated pool with fallback to hosted small-flan if latency > 350ms p90.

kai: Quick validation checklist I ran: weights checksum ✅, tokenizer vocab size 50288 (after special token add) ✅, model config `max_position_embeddings` is 2048 — we must enforce `max_total_tokens <= 2048` for prompt+gen or use sliding window for longer contexts.

sara: small workaround for token mismatch in runtime: in model adapter init do:
```
if tokenizer.eos_token_id not in (expected_list):
  tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token':'</s>'})
  model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))
```
This prevents the truncation bug in evals.

deploy-bot: Canary dry-run finished: 20 requests simulated, p50=65ms, p90=310ms, mem=14GB. No OOMs. Logs: `no-cache-hits` for prefix since key namespace differs -> we should seed prefix cache for common prompts.

ryan: Good catch on cache. For prefix caching we need to ensure tokenizer normalization matches cache key generation (lowercasing, whitespace). I'll add a quick normalizer step in cache key fn.

anika: Also pinging @morgan @kai for code review on PR #5123 (model-adapter flan-2x fixes). It's got the tokenizer remap + config defaults. Please review before EOD PST.

morgan: Reviewing now. Can we also add an automated config validation that rejects `max_total_tokens` > model.max_position_embeddings at config load time? That'll avoid bad rollouts.

kai: Agree — I'll add that validator. Will also add a small unit test that loads the weights path and ensures `model.config` fields are present.

sara: one more gotcha: some of our prompt templates include trailing spaces that previously changed prefix cache keys. I'll open a tiny docs PR to call out canonical prompt sanitization.

morgan: Plan: merge PR once reviews in, run 1-hour canary at 5%, monitor p95 latency and cache hit rate, then ramp to 25% if stable. I'll update the rollout doc after the canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

anika: noted — will post a brief after-canary checklist in #eng-runtime.

kai: tagging follow-ups: create ticket for seeding prefix cache for top-100 prompts, and an infra task to expose `max_generated_tokens` in console UI.

morgan: Nice. Closing loop — will update here with canary results later today.
thread_text: Onboarding Flan-2x into Dedicated pool: weights, tokenizer, and serving knobs (batching/cache/scheduler/max tokens)
